name: Harness Engineering: Deterministic Simulation Testing & Virtualized Clocks
tagline: Intercept every source of non-determinism behind an abstraction layer driven by one seed `S_0` and a virtualized monotonic clock that warps past idle time.
purpose: Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) replaces all non-deterministic OS syscalls—clocks, network sockets, disk I/O, and PRNG—with a single-seeded deterministic event loop so distributed bugs reproduce bit-for-bit.

spark.summary: Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST) replaces all non-deterministic OS syscalls—clocks, network sockets, disk I/O, and PRNG—with a single-seeded deterministic event loop so distributed bugs reproduce bit-for-bit.
spark.keyTakeaway: If replicas diverge under asymmetric network delays, intercept every source of non-determinism behind an abstraction layer driven by one seed `S_0` and a virtualized monotonic clock that warps past idle time.
spark.byteSummary:
Distributed consensus bugs (split-brain under asymmetric partitions, fsync-reordering corruption) often occur only once in 10,000 cluster-hours. Real-world integration tests are too slow and non-deterministic to reproduce them reliably.

**Deterministic Simulation Testing (DST)**—pioneered by FoundationDB and TigerBeetle—runs an entire multi-node distributed cluster inside a **single-threaded deterministic event loop**. All time (`VirtualClock`), randomness (`PRNG(S_0)`), network packets, and disk writes pass through a simulated I/O layer.

Because the simulator warps its virtual clock straight to the next scheduled event without `sleep()`, 1 hour of simulated network partitions executes in milliseconds—and any invariant failure reproduces 100% deterministically from its 64-bit seed.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Harness Engineering: Deterministic Simulation Testing & Virtualized Clocks without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If replicas diverge under asymmetric network delays, intercept every source of non-determinism behind an abstraction layer driven by one seed `S_0` and a virtualized monotonic clock that warps past idle time.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Reference Implementation
learningJourney.purpose: Implement the core DeterministicSimulator event loop with seeded PRNG and strict (ts, seq) heap ordering.

sectionDiagram.title: Reference Implementation

cards.label: No Global RNG
cards.detail: Never call global random or os.urandom inside simulated nodes—route all randomness through self.rng.

cards.label: Virtual Time Jumps
cards.detail: self.now_ms jumps directly to the next event timestamp without sleeping real wall time.

cards.label: Callback Isolation
cards.detail: Each callback executes atomically on the single thread, eliminating data-race nondeterminism.

sectionDiagram.summary: Seeded PRNG and a (now_ms, seq) min-heap advance virtual time instantaneously while executing callbacks deterministically.

prerequisites.title: Consistency & Consensus Replication (Raft / Paxos)
prerequisites.summary: Fault-tolerant replication protocols (Raft, Multi-Paxos, Quorum) that keep distributed state consistent across node crashes and network partitions using majority quorums (2f+1) and monotonic term numbers.

prerequisites.title: Clock Skew & NTP Backward Jumps: Monotonic Timers vs. Wall-Clock Leases
prerequisites.summary: Wall-clock timestamps (time.time() / System.currentTimeMillis()) can jump backward or forward during NTP steps; local timers must use CLOCK_MONOTONIC while distributed leases require server-side TTLs and monotonic fencing tokens.
